title: Coefficient and geometric naturality of Cartier realizations
statement: Fix a prime l and finite E/Q_l, with the interfaces [def-amb-cartier-kummer-data]. Assume every finite positive quotient coefficient is killed by an l-power. Let κ be any normalized ordinary boundary family and c any published pro-etale Cartier family satisfying CartierKummerRealization κ c. Then κ satisfies CartierEtaleKummerReduction, c satisfies CartierKummerBaseChange for all Cartier-preserving pullbacks, and c satisfies CartierKummerReduction for every pair a≤b of positive quotient levels. This is naturality of an already realized class, not its existence or its uniqueness.

proof.text: Choose a common annihilating exponent for any two coefficient levels. Supported constants have stalk the coefficient ring on the divisor and zero elsewhere; root lines are locally free of rank one. Thus both have degree-zero K-flat scalar extensions. Tensor associativity identifies successive extension from the residue ring with direct extension. Constants and root tensors give the specified coefficient maps; boundary naturality and uniqueness give SupportedKummerScalar for the two etale arrows.

At a common annihilating exponent use the GeoCartierScalarCompatibility supplied by sk-lem-geo-cartier; its units already have Hom bijections against every unbounded pro-etale test object. Boundary uniqueness and quotient-unit normalization identify the source comparison. Conjugate the target unit by the two finite Tate comparisons and the restricted-scalar inverse. Composition with these isomorphisms preserves each Hom bijection. On local pure root tensors the normalized comparisons identify this with the published quotient-coefficient map; tensor sheafification determines the unit globally. Conjugate the GeoCartier Ext square and substitute the two realization equations. This gives CartierKummerReduction, including a=b.

A Cartier-preserving pullback preserves the dual ideal line with its complementary frame. Use the ordinary supported Kummer pullback square, the invertible closed exchange and the finite Tate descent pullback square. The adjunction mate between comparison and inverse image intertwines the supported-source and Tate comparisons. Conjugate the ordinary Ext square to obtain CartierKummerBaseChange, retaining both constant-unit and root normalizations. No coefficient-flatness or geometric-flatness hypothesis is used.

lean.statement:
theorem cartier_kummer_naturality
    (hkill : ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ r : ℕ,
      ((l ^ (r + 1) : ℕ) : finiteTateCoefficient l E n) = 0)
    (κ : CartierEtaleKummerFamily l E) (c : CartierKummerFamily l E)
    (hκ : CartierEtaleKummerNormalization l E κ)
    (hc : CartierKummerRealization l E κ c) :
    CartierEtaleKummerReduction l E κ ∧
      CartierKummerBaseChange l E c ∧ CartierKummerReduction l E c
